points.description: Asynchronous transmission: each character is sent as its own unit, framed by a start bit and a stop bit (simple/cheap, lower transmission rate).
points.partial_credit: Half if only says characters are sent individually or only mentions start/stop bits without a clear contrast, or just says it is slower/simple.

points.description: Synchronous transmission: many characters grouped into a continuous stream/frames (delimited by SYN or flag), needing sender–receiver synchronization, more complex but higher transmission rate.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says data is sent in blocks/frames or only says it is faster/needs synchronization, without the fuller idea.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating the central contrast: asynchronous sends single characters with start/stop bits, synchronous sends characters pooled in frames/continuous stream with synchronization. Give part marks for vague or one-sided answers (e.g., only describing one mode, or only saying one is faster). Wrong extra remarks do not cost marks unless they swap the two modes.
